title: Saw Meshy T2 just launched low-poly mesh generation. compared the same assets to Tripo Smart Mesh P1.0.
author: Dangerous-Guava-9232
selftext:
For some time now, I have been using Tripo AI Smart Mesh P 1.0. To see how they differed, I ran the same input through both.

Setup: Same input images, tested at 5K, 10K, 15K and 20K faces.

Findings:

Meshy T2 (on the left of the pic above): Excellent outcomes at 5K faces, however over 10K, edge flow significantly deteriorates. Small accessories, fingers, and weapon pieces are examples of fine details that are lost or cause mesh defects. For 5K faces, it took roughly 45 seconds.

Tripo Smart Mesh P1.0 (on the right of the pic above): Consistent quality over the whole spectrum. At greater face counts, there is no abrupt decline. For 5K faces, it took roughly 5 seconds.

the difference in speed changes my testing process. An added feature for hero assets is the ability to test 20K face variants without changing tools.

Happy to share more comparison shots if anyone is interested. Anyone else tried both? Want to hear other thoughts.

comments.author: Firewall0110
comments.body:
I have similar results. Your images hint at it but without your source concept I can't say for myself but I find that meshy gives a poor representation of my concepts. My game is ship based and Franky the from identical concept work, meshy results are just unacceptable deviations from the source. Tripo has great hard edge representation and is very very true to the source.

I have a year long meshy subscription and ill still use it for background assets, set dressings, and tilesets but for more complicated geometry I'm willing to pay the API fees for tripo.

replies.author: thatkidnamedrocky
replies.body: sighh i just paid for a year sub for Meshy and kinda regret it after seeing Tripo

comments.author: astanar
comments.body: I find that meshy is just much better at “low poly” texturing. The models are roughly the same, but tripo always ends up applying a HD texture while the image provided clearly shows low poly stuff. Meshy gets the texture right.
